name: Marcus LeGrand
reasoning: Chair 2 ("strengthen civil rights enforcement and address systemic discrimination") rather than chair 3 ("maintain current civil rights laws while promoting equal opportunity"). The load-bearing evidence is LeGrand's own May 2025 Deschutes County voters' pamphlet statement, which under the heading "With your vote, I will continue to" pledges to "Promote equity-focused policies and student-centered programming" — a first-person, forward-looking commitment to enact equity policy, which is more than chair 3's maintenance of existing law. The same statement says "I bring expertise in equity, mental health, and inclusive programming." Context establishing which half of this topic's axis that equity language refers to (biography, not itself a stance): the listed occupation is "Professor, Afrocentric Program Coordinator" and the prior governmental experience includes the district's "Restorative Justice & Equity" role and the Oregon Department of Education "AABSS Advisory Group" (African American/Black Student Success) — i.e. the racial-inequality half. Not chair 1, which requires equity mandates across all institutions plus reparations; neither has been advocated. REVIEWER CAVEAT: this rests on a campaign pledge, not a policy record, and "promote equity-focused policies" carries no enforcement mechanism — a reviewer could defensibly argue chair 3. Resolution 1985 (Feb 11 2025, 7-0) is deliberately NOT cited as support: see wave6-school-z1-4-NOTES.md for why that resolution cannot discriminate chairs 2 and 3.
